This brand (commercial agreement materials public performance materials, 2025 sample): ~44.9% of rooms from Choice Privileges contribution. Enterprise / CRS booking mix ~61.6% in the same sample.

blocks.title: Weekly-Stay Studio Ops
blocks.body: Operators who manage kitchenettes and weekly billing—not midscale breakfast execution.

blocks.title: Relative Positioning
blocks.body: Suburban Studios sits at the economy extended-stay base of Choice's longer-stay ladder—studio kitchenettes and weekly billing below MainStay residential extended and Everhome's newer extended prototype—not nightly midscale select-service or upscale full-service conversion targets.

blocks.title: Economy Extended-Stay Studio
blocks.body: Suburban Studios creates owner value as an economy extended-stay studio where weekly demand can outrun pure transient economy rate assumptions. Underwrite conversion or prototype capital, kitchenette utilities, and labor against Choice extended-stay peers. The affiliation works best when the operating team can sustain brand-level quality and guest experience after opening. Weaker when affiliation is modeled on rates the studio product will not earn.

blocks.title: Weekly-Stay Employment Corridor
blocks.body: Employment corridors fit Suburban when weekly-stay demand from contractors and relocating workers is durable. Diligence conversion capital, competitive set, and labor before modeling Choice loyalty lift for the corridor. Owner value holds when underwriting prices economy extended-stay honestly for the asset. Weaker when markets lack lasting weekly demand after affiliation.

blocks.title: Kitchenette Conversion
blocks.body: Kitchenette conversions create owner value when the physical product can support longer stays without full-service capital. Confirm conversion PIP, capital for kitchens and laundry, and operator readiness for extended-stay standards after cutover. Weaker when underwriting ignores kitchenette refresh costs or treats affiliation as only a cosmetic light reflag.

Extended-stay studios at economy-extended price versus MainStay residential upscale extended—kitchenette FF&E and weekly billing.
Sites near industrial, medical, and project corridors where guests stay by the week, not the night.
Conversions of older studio product needing Choice systems; public performance materials ~44.9% loyalty / ~61.6% enterprise with 6.0% royalty.

Economy extended-stay studio conversions near employment centers, medical corridors, and project-driven demand where guests stay by the week with in-suite kitchenettes—owners seeking Choice platform distribution at leaner extended-stay economics than MainStay residential upscale extended.

Why owners choose Suburban: affordable extended stay with kitchenettes.
Guest promise: studio space for weekly and monthly guests on a budget.
Economics: 6.0% royalty at economy-extended positioning—compare MainStay and Everhome.
Operations: kitchenette FF&E, weekly housekeeping cadence, utility costs.
Fit: extended-stay operators accepting economy average daily rate—not Cambria or Comfort transient.

Conversion PIP scope for Suburban Studios should align conversion and new construction; weekly rate mix; lean extended-stay operations.—sequence FF&E, signage, systems, and breakfast/F&B (if required) with financing and brand approval gates.

blocks.title: In-Suite Kitchen
blocks.body:
Typical consideration: Kitchenette or full kitchen with appliances, ware, and ventilation per prototype.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm FF&E, utilities, fire/life safety, and wear reserves.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Weekly housekeeping cadence affects wear.

blocks.title: Lobby / Public Space
blocks.body:
Typical consideration: Arrival, seating, and brand-appropriate public space.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm layout, FF&E, and conversion flexibility.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Upscale/collection may require higher design investment.

blocks.title: Guestroom Standards
blocks.body:
Typical consideration: Bedding, bath, work area, finishes, and FF&E per prototype.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm PIP scope, procurement, and room mix.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Conversions often need project-specific review.

blocks.title: Fitness / Pool
blocks.body:
Typical consideration: Fitness and/or pool where prototype requires.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm minimum size, equipment, and operating cost.
Typical status: May Apply
Notes to confirm: Economy brands may have reduced requirements.

blocks.title: Signage / Exterior
blocks.body:
Typical consideration: Brand signage and exterior identity.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm monument, façade, and permitting.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Radisson-family flags have distinct identity packages.

blocks.title: Technology / Systems
blocks.body:
Typical consideration: PMS, CRS, loyalty, Wi-Fi, and reporting integrations.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm cutover timeline, training, and recurring tech fees.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Mandatory Choice stack beyond headline royalty.

blocks.title: Training / QA
blocks.body:
Typical consideration: Opening checklist, Choice University training, and QA inspections.
Owner planning consideration: Confirm inspection fees, remediation, and ongoing QA cadence.
Typical status: Typically Expected
Notes to confirm: Upscale QA burden exceeds economy.

blocks.title: Evaluation
blocks.body: Screen market tier, weekly demand depth, kitchen layout, capital envelope, and whether Suburban Studios' economy extended-stay model matches the physical asset and operator—not whether it merely needs a Choice flag. Confirm employment-corridor fit and utility economics before committing conversion capital.

blocks.title: Conversion Design
blocks.body: Shape conversion design around studio kitchenette prototype, weekly billing infrastructure, and Choice systems requirements. Align PIP, appliance scope, and operator capacity with extended-stay wear assumptions; avoid treating Suburban as a light reflag that underfunds kitchens or housekeeping rhythm.

blocks.title: Pre-Opening
blocks.body: Sequence lean staffing hires, extended-stay training, PMS/CRS/loyalty cutover, and weekly-rate readiness with design sign-off. Budget time for commercial setup and QA touchpoints. Operators typically lead daily pre-opening execution while owners fund kitchen FF&E and confirm milestones with brand development.

blocks.title: Opening
blocks.body: Execute opening with weekly rate integrity, channel mix discipline, and early QA across the first 90–120 days. Guest-facing teams should deliver consistent extended-stay basics while Choice systems stabilize. This brand is strongest when the ownership team can support the physical product, service model, and operating expectations that make the affiliation credible.

blocks.title: Ramp-Up
blocks.body: During ramp-up, calibrate loyalty contribution, seasonal project demand, and weekly retail tuning against appliance wear and utility trends—not only occupancy headlines. Revisit kitchen replacement reserves, housekeeping labor, and guest-quality indicators carefully before year-one capital surprises force reactive spend.

blocks.title: Ongoing
blocks.body: On an ongoing basis, maintain capex planning for kitchens and FF&E, brand initiatives, and portfolio benchmarks inside Choice reporting rhythms. Reassess operator fit when employment corridors shift—Suburban value depends on sustained weekly operations plus reliable system participation.

Guests: Extended-stay studios for weekly and monthly guests.

Owners: extended-stay economy Choice flag with portfolio distribution and standards clarity.

Underwrite contribution after fees, loyalty costs, and channel mix versus comp set.

blocks.title: Owner outcomes
blocks.body: Owners buy Suburban Studios for economy extended-stay studio economics—outcomes depend on weekly-stay demand, kitchenette product delivery, and disciplined operating costs.

blocks.title: Extended-Stay Midscale Conversion
blocks.body: Suburban Studios creates owner value where extended-stay demand can stabilize occupancy versus pure transient midscale—underwrite length-of-stay mix, kitchenette utility, and conversion capital against Choice extended-stay peers before modeling affiliation lift.

blocks.title: Employment Corridor Portfolio Play
blocks.body: Employment corridors fit Suburban when durable weekly and midweek demand can fill an efficient extended-stay box—owners gain Choice channel scale when labor rhythms and brand standards stay inside underwriting for the corridor.

blocks.title: Purpose-Built Prototype Development
blocks.body: Purpose-built Suburban prototypes suit sponsors who want disciplined extended-stay capital without overbuilding public space—value holds when construction costs, operator readiness, and Choice economics are modeled to weekly-stay rate support peers.

blocks.title: Third-Party Operator-Led
blocks.body: Suburban works with operators who can run extended-stay housekeeping rhythms and Choice systems cutover—sponsors need affiliation lift and financing credibility while keeping kitchenette utility, conversion scope, and staffing inside underwriting.

Conversion of older extended-stay to Suburban prototype.

Weekly-stay demand near industrial or medical employment.

Portfolio extended-stay at lower capex than MainStay.

Markets that cannot support extended-stay economy average daily rate or required amenity stack.

OTA-heavy mix without modeling net after retail and member discounts.
